transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-02
Start: 15:00 EST / 20:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Jupiter InfoSec), Liam O'Neal (Cloud Architect), Daniel Ruiz (Vendor Risk), Priya Menon (Legal)

Summary:
Jupiter Financial runs EU and US operations with strict data residency and long-term log retention requirements. This call walks through the customer's vendor security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ style) with emphasis on encryption/KMS, audit logs, SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SCIM/RBAC controls, and private deployment options. Redwood AE/SE clarified evidence artifacts, retention windows, and next steps to deliver a CAIQ mapping spreadsheet and redacted compliance reports.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 status and how/redwood produces artifacts
- RBAC and SSO integration (Okta SAML + SCIM provisioning)
- Audit logs: retention, immutability, and export for customer audits
- Encryption at rest (KMS/HSM) and key custody options (Redwood-managed KMS vs customer-managed keys/CMEK)
- Data residency and private deployment (VPC/on-prem) feasibility
- Evidence artifacts and naming conventions (policies, certificates, pentest reports)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — say hi.
[00:10] Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha here, head of infosec at Jupiter. We're focused on the SIG and CAIQ items relevant to crypto and auditability.
[00:20] Liam O'Neal: Liam, cloud arch. I want to understand the network and KMS flow, specifically if keys cross regions.
[00:27] Samir Patel: Hi all, Samir from Redwood infra — I'll try to run through the technical bits and map back to the questionnaire as we go.
[00:35] Daniel Ruiz: Daniel from vendor risk. We'll check answers against our internal risk matrix; retention windows and audit evidence are big for us.
[00:42] Priya Menon: Priya, legal. Quick note: any redacted artifacts should be mark-up safe for sharing.

[02:05] Samir Patel: Starting with compliance posture: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type II, report period June 2025 - Nov 2025. We also maintain ISO 27001 certification scoped to the hosted control plane and API surface — full scope doc we'll share.
[02:20] Aisha Khan: SOC 2 — is that Type II with auditor note and test procedures included? We need the actual test descriptions not just the opinion.
[02:28] Samir Patel: Yes, the redacted report includes the test objectives and exceptions section; we'll upload a redacted PDF. Note: we redact customer-identifying data and some internal IP addresses.
[03:12] Maya Chen: Action: we'll place doc in your secure folder, link to be shared in follow-up notes.

[04:00] Liam O'Neal: On encryption: do you support customer-managed keys (CMEK) for storage and model artifacts? If yes, what KMS providers and regions?
[04:12] Samir Patel: Short answer: yes for Private deployments and Dedicated in certain plans. For Hosted we currently offer Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys in AWS KMS. For Private/VPC we can integrate with customer KMS via AWS KMS CMKs, GCP KMS, or in-prem HSMs depending on connectivity.
[04:40] Liam O'Neal: Do keys ever leave the EU region in the EU deployment?
[04:45] Samir Patel: Our policy for EU-resident deployments pins KMS and storage to the region; keys are created in the EU region and not mirrored outside unless customer consents. I'll mark that in the CAIQ answer.

[06:10] Aisha Khan: Logging: we require immutable audit logs with 7 year retention for certain regulated lines. How does Redwood handle log immutability and export for e-discovery?
[06:22] Samir Patel: Logs are written to append-only buckets with write-once retention policies configurable per-customer in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we have standard 90-day retention in platform but we provide log export and streaming to customer S3 or SIEM. For the 7-year need, Dedicated or Private recommended — we'll document the export pathway and the retention settings.
[06:58] Daniel Ruiz: Is there an audit trail for admin actions? We need per-token, per-user action breakdowns for forensic timelines.
[07:10] Samir Patel: Yes, we capture admin events (role changes, deployments, key rotations) and these map to the audit log schema; timestamps, actor, source IP, action. We'll include sample log JSON in the artifact set.

[08:45] Priya Menon: About legal access: are there background checks or personnel security controls you can demonstrate for operators with access to keys or logs?
[08:56] Samir Patel: We have background screening policy and limited privileged access. We'll provide redacted HR process evidence and the policy doc.

[10:00] Maya Chen: On SSO/SCIM: Okta is fully supported; SAML SSO plus SCIM provisioning for user and group sync. For RBAC roles we have Admin, DevOps, Viewer, Auditor and you can create custom roles.
[10:15] Liam O'Neal: Can we restrict RBAC so auditors can see logs but not dev environments?
[10:22] Samir Patel: Yes, granular roles — Auditor role can be scoped to readonly access to audit logs and billing routes only. We'll add that mapping to the CAIQ and provide sample RBAC policy YAML.

[12:40] Aisha Khan: Pen test cadence and vulnerability disclosure — do you run annual external pentests and have bug bounty or public VDP?
[12:52] Samir Patel: Annual external pentest plus continuous automated scanning; we operate a private VDP with triage and SLA. We do not run a public bounty program but are open to enterprise programs. We'll include the latest pentest executive summary.

[14:30] Daniel Ruiz: For SIG crypto controls, we need specifics: key rotation policy, algorithm lists, and whether keys are shared across tenants.
[14:42] Samir Patel: Keys are not shared across tenants; rotation is 90 days by default for some material keys, and per-customer rotation for CMEK. Algorithms: AES-256 for at-rest, TLS1.2+ for transport; we'll add algorithms list to artifacts.

[17:05] Priya Menon: Data residency request — Jupiter wants all log exports for EU customers to stay in an EU region and for backups to be EU-only. How do you guarantee no cross-region backup?
[17:18] Samir Patel: For Private and Dedicated we can configure region-level isolation and restrict backup replication. For Hosted we offer region controls but some control-plane telemetry may be in global control plane; we can redact telemetry in artifacts. We'll capture the exact control plane flows in the follow-up diagram.

[19:50] Maya Chen: Quick note on evidence naming: we'll provide file names like redwood-soc2-report-2025-redacted.pdf, redwood-iso27001-scope-2025.docx, redwood-kms-architecture-eu.png, caiq-mapping-jupiter-2025.xlsx.
[20:05] Aisha Khan: Preferably with checksum or signed manifest so we can reference immutability.
[20:12] Samir Patel: We'll include hashes and signed manifest for delivered artifacts.

[22:30] Liam O'Neal: Network/topology question: if we run a private deployment inside our VPC, does Redwood maintain any egress to your control plane? How are updates delivered?
[22:45] Samir Patel: Private deployment options include air-gapped on-prem and VPC-connected with a control plane link. Updates can be pull-based from your environment or orchestrated through a customer-managed bastion. We'll outline the update mechanism choices in the follow-up doc.

[25:00] Daniel Ruiz: For the questionnaire, there are a few SIG items flagged as high priority: CCR-09 (encryption key custody), AL-03 (audit logging retention), and ID-07 (SSO/SCIM provisioning). Please pre-populate those.
[25:12] Samir Patel: We'll pre-fill those columns in the mapping and provide supporting artifacts.

[27:40] Aisha Khan: About log exports to our SIEM, do you support streaming in near real-time and does it include KV cache related telemetry?
[27:55] Samir Patel: We stream request and admin events; KV cache telemetry is included as operational metrics but not user data. For forensic needs we can include request traces with PII redaction.

[30:10] Priya Menon: Legal question — if we need a custom Data Processing Agreement (DPA), will Redwood accept modifications around breach notification timings and subprocessor lists?
[30:22] Maya Chen: We have a standard DPA but enterprise customers can request changes; longer negotiation sometimes needed. We'll escalate to legal and provide redlines when you send the DPA template.

[33:00] Aisha Khan: Can you confirm retention default settings for the hosted tier again?
[33:10] Samir Patel: Hosted defaults: 90 days for request logs, 30 days for some transient telemetry. Dedicated/Private you can configure per contract up to multi-year. We'll document default vs configurable choices.

[35:50] Liam O'Neal: Are there any known limitations with FIPS-compliant HSMs? We need FIPS validated crypto for some lines.
[35:58] Samir Patel: We can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs in customer-managed deployments; hosted HSMs depend on cloud provider attestation — we'll include our provider attestations.

[38:00] Daniel Ruiz: On liability and indemnities, not legal advice here, but note that our procurement team will push for contractual clauses around data breach thresholds.
[38:10] Priya Menon: Yep — we'll handle on procurement track.

[40:15] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: Samir will deliver CAIQ mapping spreadsheet and sample logs; Maya will share compressed redacted reports; schedule technical follow-up for private deployment.
[40:30] Aisha Khan: Good. Also can you include a sample RBAC policy and a small demo of log export in the next call?
[40:38] Samir Patel: Yep, demo of export + RBAC policy will be in the tech deep dive.

[41:50] Daniel Ruiz: We'll run these answers through our vendor risk tool and circle back with any follow-ups. Expect a short vendor scorecard.

[42:20] Maya Chen: Thanks folks, we'll send notes and artifact links.
[42:30] Aisha Khan: Thanks. Bye.

References / shared artifacts mentioned:
- redwood-soc2-report-2025-redacted.pdf (to be uploaded)
- redwood-iso27001-scope-2025.docx (to be uploaded)
- caiq-mapping-jupiter-2025.xlsx (Samir to create)

End of transcript.
